question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

We saw him (the more) during Hogsmeade weekend.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. the most.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs an adverb of frequency/degree modifying the verb "saw". With a single subject and no comparison between two things, the superlative degree "the most" is used. (सर्वाधिक)

◦ "More" is a comparative and needs a second element of comparison (than ...); "the more" cannot stand alone here.

◦ Correct: We saw him the most during Hogsmeade weekend.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "the many" is a determiner used with plural countable nouns (the many people), not with a verb.

• Option 3 "the bigger" is an adjective in the comparative degree and cannot modify the verb "saw".

• Option 4 is wrong because the bracketed part "the more" is grammatically incomplete, so a correction IS required.

NOTE

• Degrees: much – more – most; little – less – least; many – more – most.

• "The more ... the more ..." is a valid double-comparative structure (The more you read, the more you learn), but it needs both clauses.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

He teaches me algebraic and geometry twice a week.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. taught me algebra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Algebraic" is an adjective; the object of "teach" must be a noun, i.e. algebra, to be parallel with the noun "geometry". (बीजगणित)

◦ The indirect object of a verb must be in the objective case — "me", not the subject pronoun "I".

◦ Correct: He taught me algebra and geometry twice a week.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "taught I algebra" wrongly uses the subjective pronoun "I" as an object.

• Option 3 "teach me algebraic" keeps the adjective "algebraic" and also gives a plain-form verb that does not agree with the singular subject "He".

• Option 4 is wrong because the sentence does contain an error ("algebraic").

NOTE

• Subject pronouns: I, we, you, he, she, it, they; Object pronouns: me, us, you, him, her, it, them.

• Only Option 2 supplies the noun "algebra"; note that it also shifts the tense to the past, so the improvement must be read as replacing the whole underlined segment "teaches me algebraic".

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

I mean that is a remarkable finding.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. noticeable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Remarkable means worthy of attention, striking, extraordinary — something that gets noticed. (उल्लेखनीय)

◦ Noticeable means easily seen or observed, attracting notice — the closest synonym. (ध्यान देने योग्य)

◦ Correct: I mean that is a noticeable (remarkable) finding.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Dim — faint, not bright; dull (धुंधला) — an antonym in sense.

• Standard — usual, ordinary, average (सामान्य) — opposite of remarkable.

• Subtle — delicate, not obvious, hard to notice (सूक्ष्म) — the opposite of noticeable.

NOTE

• Synonyms of remarkable: extraordinary, notable, striking, conspicuous, phenomenal.

• Antonyms of remarkable: ordinary, commonplace, unremarkable, insignificant.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

A person who likes or admires women
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Philogynist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Philogynist = a person who likes, admires or is fond of women (Greek *philo-* = loving + *gyne* = woman). (नारी-प्रेमी)

◦ The prefix philo-/phil- always means "love of": philanthropist, philologist, bibliophile.

◦ Correct: A person who likes or admires women is called a philogynist.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Polyglot — a person who knows and can use several languages. (बहुभाषाविद)

• Misogynist — a person who hates women (*miso-* = hatred); the exact opposite. (नारी-द्वेषी)

• Conversationalist — a person who is good at or fond of conversation.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions: Misogamist — one who hates marriage; Misanthrope — one who hates mankind; Philanthropist — one who loves and helps mankind; Bibliophile — a lover of books.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To pick holes in someone's coat
option_2: To deceive someone for personal gain
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To find fault with someone.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to pick holes in someone's coat" means to find fault with somebody, to criticise or point out defects. (किसी में दोष निकालना)

◦ The shorter form "pick holes in" is used for criticising an argument or plan.

◦ Correct usage: Instead of helping, he kept picking holes in my coat at every meeting.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "To discharge one's duty well" is expressed by idioms such as "to rise to the occasion" / "to do one's bit".

• "To deceive someone for personal gain" corresponds to "to take someone for a ride".

• "To aspire for something difficult" corresponds to "to aim at the moon" / "to cry for the moon".

NOTE

• Similar idioms: to find fault with — to criticise; to nitpick — to fuss over trivial faults; to run someone down — to speak ill of someone.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

For example, the parent mountain/ of Mont Blanc, the/ high peak in the Alps, is the Mount Everest.
option_2: high peak in the Alps, is the Mount Everest.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. high peak in the Alps, is the Mount Everest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The definite article "the" is not used before the names of individual mountain peaks — Mount Everest, Mount Fuji, Kanchenjunga. ("The" is used only with mountain *ranges*: the Alps, the Himalayas.)

◦ So "is the Mount Everest" must be "is Mount Everest".

◦ Correct: For example, the parent mountain of Mont Blanc, the high peak in the Alps, is Mount Everest.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "of Mont Blanc, the" is correct — no article is used with the single peak Mont Blanc, and "the" belongs to the following noun phrase "high peak".

• Option 4 "For example, the parent mountain" is a correct noun phrase with a proper definite article.

• Option 1 "No error" is wrong because the error in the third segment does exist.

NOTE

• Article rules: the with ranges (the Alps, the Andes), rivers (the Ganga), oceans (the Pacific), deserts (the Sahara); no article with single peaks (Everest), continents, countries (except the USA, the UK), and single islands.

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym to substitute the bracketed word in the given sentence.

For high-moisture areas, like kitchens and baths or where (frequent) cleaning is required, use only oil-based.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. seldom.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Frequent means happening often, occurring at short intervals. (बार-बार होने वाला)

◦ Seldom means rarely, not often — the opposite idea of frequency. (कदाचित/विरले ही)

◦ Correct: For high-moisture areas ... or where seldom cleaning is required, use only oil-based.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Confirmed — established as true, firmly settled (पुष्ट) — not related to frequency.

• Dawdle — to waste time, to move slowly (आलस्य करना) — a verb, not an antonym of frequent.

• Constant — continuous, unceasing (निरंतर) — a synonym of frequent, hence wrong.

NOTE

• Frequency adverbs from most to least: always > usually > often/frequently > sometimes > seldom/rarely > never.

• Antonyms of frequent: rare, occasional, infrequent, sporadic, scarce.

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Glamour
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Dullness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Glamour means an attractive, exciting or fascinating quality; charm and allure. (आकर्षण/मोहकता)

◦ Dullness means the state of being boring, drab and lacking brightness or interest — the direct opposite. (नीरसता)

◦ Correct: The film had none of the glamour she expected; only dullness.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Charm — the power of pleasing or attracting (आकर्षण) — a synonym of glamour.

• Magnanimous — generous and forgiving, especially towards a rival (उदार) — unrelated in meaning.

• Appeal — attraction or interest (आकर्षण) — again a synonym, not an antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of glamour: allure, fascination, magnetism, enchantment, charisma.

• Antonyms of glamour: dullness, plainness, drabness, repulsiveness.

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Graetar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word is misspelt; the correct spelling is Greater (the comparative of "great"). (अधिक बड़ा)

◦ "Great" keeps the -ea- vowel pair and simply adds -er: great → greater; the printed "ae" and the ending "-ar" are both wrong.

◦ Correct: This year's profit is greater than last year's.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Rocking — correctly spelt; "rock" + "-ing" (no doubling after a single final consonant preceded by a short vowel in a one-syllable word ending in -ck).

• Frame — correctly spelt noun/verb meaning a border or structure.

• Decrease — correctly spelt; note the -ea- in the second syllable (de-crease).

NOTE

• Commonly misspelt comparatives: greater, heavier, happier (y → i + er), bigger (double consonant), later vs latter.

• Frequently tested spellings in SSC: necessary, occurrence, embarrass, maintenance, privilege, separate.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Add fuel to the fire
option_1: When an attempt fails and it's time to start all over
option_2: Having to start all over again
option_3: To make an argument or bad situation worse
option_4: A mistake made in something you are trying to achieve
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To make an argument or bad situation worse.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "add fuel to the fire" (also "add fuel to the flames") means to do or say something that makes an already bad situation, quarrel or anger even worse. (जले पर नमक छिड़कना / आग में घी डालना)

◦ It is used when an action intensifies an existing conflict rather than settling it.

◦ Correct usage: His sarcastic remark only added fuel to the fire during the argument.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "When an attempt fails and it's time to start all over" is the sense of "back to square one".

• "Having to start all over again" is expressed by "back to the drawing board".

• "A mistake made in something you are trying to achieve" corresponds to "a slip-up" / "to drop the ball".

NOTE

• Similar idioms: to stir up a hornet's nest — to cause trouble; to pour oil on troubled waters — to calm a situation (opposite sense); to rub salt into the wound — to worsen someone's pain.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Do you think I'd rather / be stuck in a room with that old / toad or be played Quidditch?
option_3: be stuck in a room with that old
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. toad or be played Quidditch?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Would rather" is always followed by the bare infinitive (V1) — "I'd rather be stuck ... or play Quidditch". (क्रिया का मूल रूप)

◦ "Be played" is a passive form and is wrong here because the speaker performs the action; also, both alternatives after "rather ... or" must be parallel.

◦ Correct: Do you think I'd rather be stuck in a room with that old toad or play Quidditch?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Do you think I'd rather" is correct — "I'd" is the contraction of "I would".

• Option 3 "be stuck in a room with that old" is correct — a bare infinitive "be" after "would rather".

• Option 4 "No error" is wrong because the third segment does contain a voice/parallelism error.

NOTE

• Structures with bare infinitive: would rather, had better, rather than, sooner than, modal verbs (can, may, must).

• "Would rather ... than ..." (I would rather walk than wait); "prefer ... to ..." (I prefer tea to coffee).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Nickel or brass can cause an allergic reaction when in ______ with human skin .
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. contact.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed collocation is "in contact with", meaning touching or in communication with something. (संपर्क में)

◦ The sentence is about a metal touching the skin, so "in contact with human skin" is the only meaningful fit.

◦ Correct: Nickel or brass can cause an allergic reaction when in contact with human skin.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Surface — the outer layer of something; the phrase "in surface with" does not exist in English.

• Accordance — "in accordance with" means in agreement with a rule or law, not physical touching.

• Parallel — "in parallel with" means at the same time as / alongside, which does not suit an allergic reaction.

NOTE

• Useful "in + noun + with" phrases: in contact with, in accordance with, in line with, in touch with, in comparison with, in conflict with.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Land management choices also affect the amount of carbon stored on trees.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. carbon stored on trees.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Carbon is held inside the wood and tissue of a tree, so the correct preposition is "in", not "on". ("on" would mean resting on the surface.)

◦ The standard scientific collocation is carbon stored in trees / stored in soil.

◦ Correct: Land management choices also affect the amount of carbon stored in trees.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "also affect the amount of" is correct — the plural subject "choices" takes the plural verb "affect".

• Option 4 "Land management choices" is a correctly formed plural noun phrase.

• Option 2 "No error" is wrong because the preposition error does exist.

NOTE

• in = inside/within (water in the glass); on = on the surface (a book on the table); at = a point (at the gate).

• Do not confuse affect (verb — to influence) with effect (noun — result).

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

(Then got of on) a station in the very heart of London.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. They got off at.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb for leaving a train/bus is "get off" (with double 'f'); "of" is a preposition and cannot be used here.

◦ With a station as a specific point, English uses the preposition "at" — got off at a station.

◦ Correct: They got off at a station in the very heart of London.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is wrong because "Then got of on" has no subject and misuses "of".

• Option 3 "They got of by" repeats the wrong word "of" and adds an unsuitable preposition "by".

• Option 4 "They got off on" uses the wrong preposition; "get off on" is an informal idiom meaning to enjoy something.

NOTE

• Travel phrasal verbs: get on/get off a bus, train, plane; get in/get out of a car or taxi.

• Place prepositions: at a station/bus stop, in a city, on a street.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

My friends, being incredibly nerdy linguists, ______ to make fun of the syntax.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. decided.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a verb that can take a to-infinitive as its object. Decide is regularly followed by "to + V1": *decide to do something*. (निर्णय लेना)

◦ Meaning-wise, linguists choosing to make fun of the syntax fits perfectly with "decided".

◦ Correct: My friends, being incredibly nerdy linguists, decided to make fun of the syntax.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Braided — plaited hair or strands together (चोटी बनाना); it is transitive and cannot take "to make".

• Stalked — followed or pursued stealthily (पीछा करना); it takes a direct object, not a to-infinitive.

• Traded — exchanged goods (व्यापार करना); "traded to make fun" is meaningless.

NOTE

• Verbs followed by to-infinitive: decide, agree, refuse, promise, hope, want, plan, manage, offer.

• Verbs followed by gerund (V-ing): enjoy, avoid, mind, finish, suggest, admit, consider.

question: Four sentences are given, out of which three have spelling errors. Choose the sentence with all correctly spelt words.
option_1: The extended phenotype is noticeable when we look at parasites.
option_2: The Secretary requested to be informed only as necesary to perform his job.
option_3: They predicted a similarlly miniscule drop for September.
option_4: Moving between floors, their journey seems both improbable and inevitible.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The extended phenotype is noticeable when we look at parasites.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Every word in Option 1 is correctly spelt — note noticeable, which keeps the -e- of "notice" before "-able" to preserve the soft /s/ sound.

◦ Phenotype and parasites are also spelt correctly in this sentence.

◦ Correct: The extended phenotype is noticeable when we look at parasites.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 has "necesary"; the correct spelling is necessary (one 'c', double 's').

• Option 3 has "similarlly"; the correct spelling is similarly (similar + ly).

• Option 4 has "inevitible"; the correct spelling is inevitable (-able, not -ible).

NOTE

• Keep the silent 'e' before -able after soft c/g: noticeable, manageable, changeable, serviceable.

• High-frequency SSC spellings: necessary, occasion, accommodation, embarrassment, questionnaire, inevitable.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

They bought ______ tickets instead from a sleepy-looking guard.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. their.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank comes before the noun "tickets" and shows possession, so a possessive adjective is required: their = belonging to them. (उनका/उनके)

◦ Their (possessive) must not be confused with there (place) or they're (they are).

◦ Correct: They bought their tickets instead from a sleepy-looking guard.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• There — an adverb of place or an introductory subject (There is a book); it cannot modify a noun.

• Dare — a verb/noun meaning to have the courage to do something; meaningless before "tickets".

• Dire — an adjective meaning extremely serious or urgent (dire consequences); it does not fit the context of buying tickets.

NOTE

• Homophone triplet: their (possessive) / there (place) / they're (they are).

• Other common homophones: your–you're, its–it's, whose–who's, principal–principle, stationary–stationery.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Indonesian police fired warning shots, tear gas and water cannon to try and ______ the crowd.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Disperse.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Disperse (verb) means to scatter or drive away in different directions — exactly what police do to a crowd with tear gas and water cannon. (तितर-बितर करना)

◦ The blank follows "to try and", so a verb is needed; only "disperse" is a verb among the options.

◦ Correct: Indonesian police fired warning shots, tear gas and water cannon to try and disperse the crowd.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Discrete — an adjective meaning separate and distinct (पृथक); do not confuse it with "discreet" (careful, tactful).

• Delimit — a verb meaning to fix the boundaries or limits of something (परिसीमन करना); it does not suit a crowd.

• Deleterious — an adjective meaning harmful or damaging (हानिकारक); an adjective cannot follow "to try and".

NOTE

• Synonyms of disperse: scatter, dispel, dissipate, break up, drive away.

• Antonyms of disperse: gather, assemble, collect, congregate.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

Fit to drink
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Potable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Potable means safe or fit to drink (from Latin *potare* = to drink). (पीने योग्य)

◦ It is used chiefly of water: *potable water* = drinking water.

◦ Correct: Villagers demanded a regular supply of potable water.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Ostensible — apparent or stated but perhaps not true (दिखावटी).

• Deplorable — shockingly bad, deserving strong condemnation (निंदनीय).

• Liable — legally responsible, or likely to do something (उत्तरदायी).

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions: Edible — fit to be eaten; Potable — fit to drink; Legible — able to be read; Audible — able to be heard; Inflammable — easily set on fire.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym to substitute the bracketed word in the given sentence.

Spreading from the ports, Formosan termites began a (subterranean) colonization of the country.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Underground.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Subterranean means existing, occurring or situated under the earth's surface (Latin *sub* = under + *terra* = earth). (भूमिगत)

◦ Underground carries exactly the same meaning, so it substitutes perfectly.

◦ Correct: Formosan termites began an underground (subterranean) colonization of the country.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Terrestrial — relating to the earth or to dry land (as opposed to water or air), not "below" the earth.

• Overt — done openly and not secretly (प्रकट); the opposite of hidden or underground.

• Subcutaneous — situated or applied under the skin (a subcutaneous injection), not under the ground.

NOTE

• Prefix sub- = under/below: submarine, subway, substandard, subordinate, subsoil.

• Root terra = earth: terrain, territory, terrace, extraterrestrial, Mediterranean.

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

A loud, echoing crack broke the sleepy (1) ______ like a gunshot; a cat streaked out (2) ______ a parked car and flew out of sight; a shriek, a bellowed oath and the (3) ______ of breaking (4) ______ came from the Paula's living room, and as (5) ______ this was the signal Mansi had been waiting for.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. silence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adjective "sleepy" describes a quiet, drowsy atmosphere, and a crack "like a gunshot" can only break the silence. (सन्नाटा)

◦ The collocation "break the silence" is fixed and idiomatic in English.

◦ Correct: A loud, echoing crack broke the sleepy silence like a gunshot.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Lull — a brief pause in noise or activity; "a sleepy lull" is unusual and "break the lull" is not idiomatic here.

• Blast — a loud explosive sound; a crack cannot break a blast.

• Blackout — a failure of electric power or a loss of consciousness; unrelated to sound.

NOTE

• Common collocations with silence: break the silence, maintain silence, stunned/deathly silence, an awkward silence.

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

A loud, echoing crack broke the sleepy (1) ______ like a gunshot; a cat streaked out (2) ______ a parked car and flew out of sight; a shriek, a bellowed oath and the (3) ______ of breaking (4) ______ came from the Paula's living room, and as (5) ______ this was the signal Mansi had been waiting for.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. from under.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A frightened cat hides beneath a parked car, so it "streaked out from under a parked car". (नीचे से बाहर)

◦ "From under" is a standard double preposition showing movement away from a position beneath something.

◦ Correct: A cat streaked out from under a parked car and flew out of sight.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Side under" is not an English prepositional phrase at all.

• "By under" is ungrammatical; "by" cannot combine with "under" in this way.

• "From over" would mean from a position above the car, which is illogical for a cat streaking out.

NOTE

• Other double prepositions: from behind, from beneath, from among, from across, out of, up to.

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

A loud, echoing crack broke the sleepy (1) ______ like a gunshot; a cat streaked out (2) ______ a parked car and flew out of sight; a shriek, a bellowed oath and the (3) ______ of breaking (4) ______ came from the Paula's living room, and as (5) ______ this was the signal Mansi had been waiting for.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. sound.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is a noun governed by "the ... of breaking china", and only sound works as a noun here: *the sound of breaking china*. (आवाज़)

◦ It is parallel with the other noises listed — "a shriek, a bellowed oath and the sound of breaking china".

◦ Correct: A shriek, a bellowed oath and the sound of breaking china came from the Paula's living room.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Intact — an adjective meaning undamaged and complete; it cannot follow "the".

• Flawless — an adjective meaning without any defect; again not a noun.

• Vibrant — an adjective meaning full of energy or bright; grammatically impossible in the blank.

NOTE

• "Sound" works as noun (a loud sound), verb (it sounds good) and adjective (sound sleep, sound advice).

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

A loud, echoing crack broke the sleepy (1) ______ like a gunshot; a cat streaked out (2) ______ a parked car and flew out of sight; a shriek, a bellowed oath and the (3) ______ of breaking (4) ______ came from the Paula's living room, and as (5) ______ this was the signal Mansi had been waiting for.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. china.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• China (with a small 'c') is an uncountable noun meaning fine porcelain crockery — cups, plates and saucers. (चीनी मिट्टी के बर्तन)

◦ The sound of breaking china in a living room, together with a shriek and an oath, describes crockery being smashed.

◦ Correct: ... and the sound of breaking china came from the Paula's living room.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Heart — "breaking heart" is figurative and would not produce a sound coming from a room.

• Atrocity — a cruel and violent act; "breaking atrocity" is meaningless.

• Tyre — the rubber covering of a wheel; tyres burst, they do not "break" with a shattering sound in a living room.

NOTE

• Uncountable nouns for household items: china, cutlery, crockery, furniture, luggage, stationery — they take singular verbs and no plural -s.

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

A loud, echoing crack broke the sleepy (1) ______ like a gunshot; a cat streaked out (2) ______ a parked car and flew out of sight; a shriek, a bellowed oath and the (3) ______ of breaking (4) ______ came from the Paula's living room, and as (5) ______ this was the signal Mansi had been waiting for.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. though.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The set conjunction "as though" means "as if" and introduces an imagined or supposed situation. (मानो)

◦ It is followed by a clause: *as though this was the signal ...*

◦ Correct: ... and as though this was the signal Mansi had been waiting for.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Like — informal and normally followed by a noun phrase, not the full clause used here.

• Throughout — a preposition/adverb meaning all through a period or place; it cannot introduce this clause.

• Through — a preposition meaning from one end to the other; "as through" is not an English expression.

NOTE

• As if / as though are interchangeable; with an unreal situation they may take the past subjunctive: He behaves as though he were the boss.

question: Dr. B.R Ambedkar was associated with which of the following communities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar (1891–1956) was born at Mhow (Madhya Pradesh) in the Mahar community of Maharashtra, then treated as an ‘untouchable’ caste. (महार समुदाय)

• He founded the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924), led the Mahad Satyagraha (1927) and the Kalaram Temple Entry Movement (1930) for Dalit rights.

• He was Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly and independent India’s first Law Minister; he was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1990 (posthumously).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Berar is a historical region of Vidarbha in Maharashtra, not a community.

• Santal (Santhal) is a major tribal community of Jharkhand, West Bengal and Odisha, known for the Santhal Rebellion (1855–56) led by Sidhu and Kanhu.

• Sangoi is not a recognised community associated with Ambedkar.

NOTE

• Ambedkar’s writings: ‘Annihilation of Caste’, ‘The Problem of the Rupee’, ‘Who Were the Shudras?’, ‘Buddha and His Dhamma’.

• He signed the Poona Pact (1932) with Gandhi, replacing separate electorates with reserved seats for the Depressed Classes.

question: ______ is the interest rate at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) lends money to commercial banks of the country.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Repo Rate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Repo (Repurchase) Rate is the rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks against government securities. (रेपो दर)

• A rise in the repo rate makes borrowing costlier and is used to control inflation; a cut makes credit cheaper and boosts growth.

• The repo rate is decided by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), a six-member body headed by the RBI Governor, set up under the RBI Act (amended 2016).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Reverse Repo Rate — the rate at which the RBI borrows from commercial banks, absorbing liquidity from the system.

• Base Rate — the minimum lending rate below which a bank cannot lend to its customers (now largely replaced by MCLR and the external benchmark rate).

• Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) — emergency overnight borrowing by banks from the RBI, usually 0.25% above the repo rate.

NOTE

• Quantitative tools of monetary policy: Repo, Reverse Repo, CRR, SLR, Bank Rate, OMO, MSF.

• CRR — cash kept with the RBI; SLR — liquid assets kept with the bank itself.

• The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934 and nationalised in 1949.

question: Which state was ranked first in the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban (PMAY-U) Awards 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the PMAY-U Awards 2021 (announced at the ‘Azadi@75 – New Urban India’ conference in Rajkot, Gujarat), Uttar Pradesh was adjudged the best performing state in overall implementation. (प्रधानमंत्री आवास योजना – शहरी)

• PMAY-Urban was launched on 25 June 2015 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs with the mission ‘Housing for All’.

• Its four verticals are In-situ Slum Redevelopment (ISSR), Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS), Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) and Beneficiary-Led Construction (BLC).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Madhya Pradesh and Tamil Nadu were placed among the other top-performing states in the same awards.

• PMAY-Gramin (rural) was launched on 20 November 2016 by the Ministry of Rural Development, replacing the Indira Awaas Yojana.

• Under PMAY-U, a Light House Project (LHP) was taken up in six cities to demonstrate new construction technologies.

NOTE

• Other flagship urban missions launched in 2015: Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT and HRIDAY.

• PMAY-U beneficiaries include EWS, LIG and MIG categories, and the house is preferably registered in the name of the woman of the household.

question: Bhagat Singh was executed on March 23, 1931 along with ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sukhdev and Rajguru.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev Thapar and Shivaram Rajguru were hanged at Lahore Central Jail on 23 March 1931, a day observed as Shaheed Diwas / Martyrs’ Day. (शहीद दिवस)

• They were convicted in the Lahore Conspiracy Case for the killing of Assistant Superintendent of Police J. P. Saunders (1928), done in revenge for the assault on Lala Lajpat Rai during the Simon Commission protest.

• They belonged to the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA), formed in 1928 at Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Batukeshwar Dutt threw bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly (8 April 1929) with Bhagat Singh, but was sentenced to transportation for life, not death.

• Chandra Shekhar Azad died fighting police at Alfred Park, Allahabad on 27 February 1931, before the executions.

• Bhagat Singh’s famous slogan was ‘Inquilab Zindabad’, and his prison writing is ‘Why I am an Atheist’.

NOTE

• Important dates: Shaheed Diwas – 23 March; Martyrs’ Day (Gandhi’s death) – 30 January.

• Bhagat Singh founded the Naujawan Bharat Sabha in 1926 in Lahore.

question: The blood platelets are also known as ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is thrombocytes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Platelets = thrombocytes; they are small, non-nucleated cell fragments produced from megakaryocytes in the bone marrow. (प्लेटलेट्स — थ्रोम्बोसाइट्स)

• Their main function is blood clotting (coagulation) and stopping bleeding at the site of injury.

• Normal platelet count is about 1,50,000–4,50,000 per cubic mm of blood; a sharp fall (thrombocytopenia) is seen in dengue.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Thrombin is an enzyme that converts fibrinogen into fibrin during clotting — a protein, not a cell.

• Erythrocytes are red blood cells (RBCs), which carry oxygen using haemoglobin; they live about 120 days.

• Leucocytes are white blood cells (WBCs), the body’s defence cells (neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, basophils).

NOTE

• Blood is about 55% plasma and 45% cells; plasma is roughly 90–92% water.

• RBCs are formed in the bone marrow and destroyed in the spleen (the ‘graveyard of RBCs’).

• Vitamin K is essential for the synthesis of clotting factors.

question: As of November 2022, what is the capital of India's neighbouring country Bhutan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thimphu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Thimphu is the capital and largest city of Bhutan, situated on the Wang Chhu (Raidak) river. (थिम्पू — भूटान की राजधानी)

• Bhutan’s currency is the Ngultrum; its official language is Dzongkha, and it is known as the ‘Land of the Thunder Dragon’ (Druk Yul).

• Bhutan shares borders with the Indian states of Sikkim, West Bengal, Assam and Arunachal Pradesh, and follows the development philosophy of Gross National Happiness (GNH).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Beijing is the capital of China; Dhaka is the capital of Bangladesh (currency: Taka).

• Paro is a Bhutanese town famous for the country’s only international airport and the Taktsang (Tiger’s Nest) Monastery, but it is not the capital.

• India–Bhutan relations are governed by the Treaty of Friendship of 1949, revised in 2007.

NOTE

• Capitals of India’s neighbours: Nepal – Kathmandu, Myanmar – Nay Pyi Taw, Sri Lanka – Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte (legislative) / Colombo (commercial), Pakistan – Islamabad, Afghanistan – Kabul, Maldives – Male.

• India shares its longest border with Bangladesh and the shortest with Afghanistan.

question: Which festival is celebrated when the annual harvest takes place in Assam?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Magh Bihu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Magh Bihu (Bhogali Bihu) is the harvest festival of Assam, celebrated in the month of Magh (mid-January) at the end of the harvesting season. (माघ बिहू — असम का फसल उत्सव)

• It is marked by community feasts, the building of temporary huts called ‘Meji’ and ‘Bhelaghar’, bonfires and traditional games like buffalo fighting and tekeli bhonga.

• Assam celebrates three Bihus: Bohag/Rongali Bihu (April, Assamese New Year), Magh/Bhogali Bihu (January, harvest) and Kati/Kongali Bihu (October, austerity).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Pongal is the four-day harvest festival of Tamil Nadu, dedicated to the Sun God.

• Makaravilakku is a festival at the Sabarimala temple, Kerala, observed on Makar Sankranti.

• Lohri is the harvest/bonfire festival of Punjab and Haryana, celebrated on 13 January.

NOTE

• Harvest festivals: Baisakhi – Punjab, Onam – Kerala, Nuakhai – Odisha, Wangala – Meghalaya (Garo), Ka Pomblang Nongkrem – Meghalaya (Khasi), Losoong – Sikkim.

• Other Assam festivals: Ambubachi Mela (Kamakhya Temple), Majuli Raas Mahotsav, Dehing Patkai Festival.

question: Highest population density in India according to census 2011 is in ________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Capital Territory of Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per Census 2011, the NCT of Delhi recorded the highest population density in India — about 11,320 persons per sq km. (जनसंख्या घनत्व)

• Population density = total population ÷ total area (persons per sq km); India’s average density in 2011 was 382 persons per sq km.

• Among states, Bihar had the highest density (1,106 persons/sq km), followed by West Bengal (1,028) and Kerala (860).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Chandigarh (9,258/sq km) ranks after Delhi among Union Territories.

• Arunachal Pradesh had the lowest density (17/sq km); among UTs, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands (46/sq km) was lowest.

• Madhya Pradesh had a density of about 236 persons/sq km, below the national average.

NOTE

• Census 2011 was the 15th national census and the 7th after Independence; its slogan was ‘Our Census, Our Future’.

• Census 2011 highlights: most populous state – Uttar Pradesh; least populous – Sikkim; highest literacy – Kerala (94%); lowest literacy – Bihar (61.8%); sex ratio – 943.

question: Which of the following mountain range is the oldest in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aravalli Range.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Aravalli Range is the oldest fold mountain range in India (and among the oldest in the world), formed in the Proterozoic era. (अरावली — भारत की सबसे पुरानी पर्वत श्रृंखला)

• It extends about 800 km from Delhi through Haryana and Rajasthan to Gujarat; its highest peak is Guru Shikhar (1,722 m) on Mount Abu, Rajasthan.

• The Aravallis are residual/relict mountains worn down by erosion, and act as a barrier against the spread of the Thar Desert.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Satpura and Vindhya ranges are block mountains of central India; the Narmada flows between them in a rift valley.

• Western Ghats (Sahyadri) run parallel to the west coast; the highest peak is Anamudi (2,695 m) in Kerala — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and biodiversity hotspot.

• Purvanchal Range comprises the eastern extensions of the Himalayas — the Patkai Bum, Naga, Manipur and Mizo (Lushai) hills.

NOTE

• The Himalayas are the youngest fold mountains, formed by the collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates.

• Rivers rising in the Aravallis: Banas, Luni, Sahibi.

question:
Which of the following factors can affect distribution of population?

I. Geographical factors

II. Social factors

III. Cultural factors

IV. Economic factors
solution_text:
The correct answer is I, II, III and IV.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The distribution of population is influenced by geographical, social, cultural and economic factors together — hence all four statements are correct. (जनसंख्या वितरण)

• Geographical factors include relief, climate, soil, availability of water and mineral resources — fertile plains such as the Indo-Gangetic plain are densely populated.

• Economic factors (industries, urbanisation, transport), social factors (housing, education, health facilities) and cultural/religious factors (places of religious or cultural significance) also attract or repel population.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sparsely populated areas of India: Rajasthan (desert), Arunachal Pradesh (rugged terrain), and the Himalayan cold deserts — all due to harsh geography.

• Densely populated areas: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Kerala — fertile land, water and economic opportunity.

• Push and pull factors are the standard framework used to explain migration and consequent redistribution.

NOTE

• Population distribution = the pattern of where people live; population density = number of persons per unit area.

• About 68.8% of India’s population lived in rural areas as per Census 2011.

question: The rock shelters of Bhimbetka are in the foothills of which mountains?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vindhyan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bhimbetka rock shelters lie in the foothills of the Vindhyan range in the Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh, near Bhopal. (भीमबेटका — रायसेन, मध्य प्रदेश)

• They contain prehistoric cave paintings dating from the Palaeolithic and Mesolithic periods, depicting hunting, dancing, animals and community life.

• Bhimbetka was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2003; it was brought to notice by Dr. V. S. Wakankar in 1957.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Zaskar (Zanskar) Range lies in Ladakh, to the north of the Great Himalayas.

• Pir Panjal is the largest range of the Lesser Himalayas, in Jammu & Kashmir, containing the Banihal and Pir Panjal passes.

• Satpura Range lies south of the Narmada in Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra; Dhupgarh is its highest point.

NOTE

• Other UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Madhya Pradesh: Khajuraho temples, Sanchi Buddhist monuments, and the Historic Ensembles of Dhar (Bhojeshwar) on the tentative list.

• Prehistoric painting sites for exams: Bhimbetka (MP), Jogimara caves (Chhattisgarh), Adamgarh (MP).

question: In 1900, India participated in Olympics games which was held in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Paris.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India made its first Olympic appearance at the 1900 Summer Olympics in Paris, represented by a single athlete, Norman Pritchard. (पेरिस ओलंपिक 1900)

• Pritchard won two silver medals — in the 200 m sprint and the 200 m hurdles — India’s first Olympic medals.

• India first sent an official national team in 1920 (Antwerp); the Indian Olympic Association was formed in 1927.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Athens hosted the first modern Olympics in 1896 and again in 2004.

• Berlin hosted the 1936 Olympics, where the Indian hockey team led by Dhyan Chand beat Germany 8–1 in the final.

• Tokyo hosted the Olympics in 1964 and 2020 (held in 2021), where India won 7 medals, including Neeraj Chopra’s gold in javelin.

NOTE

• India’s hockey team won 8 Olympic golds, including six in a row (1928–1956).

• Abhinav Bindra won India’s first individual Olympic gold (10 m air rifle) at Beijing 2008.

• The Olympic motto is ‘Citius, Altius, Fortius – Communiter’ (Faster, Higher, Stronger – Together).

question: Which famous Indian musician played shehnai and received Bharat Ratna in the year 2001?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ustad Bismillah Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Bismillah Khan (1916–2006) was the legendary shehnai maestro who received the Bharat Ratna in 2001. (शहनाई वादक)

• Born at Dumraon, Bihar, he made Varanasi his home and raised the shehnai from a ceremonial instrument to the concert stage.

• He played the shehnai at the Red Fort on 15 August 1947, on India’s first Independence Day, and again on the first Republic Day.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Ustad Zakir Hussain — tabla maestro; Padma Vibhushan (2023), son of Ustad Alla Rakha.

• Pandit Ravi Shankar — sitar legend; Bharat Ratna in 1999.

• Pandit Shivkumar Sharma — santoor exponent; Padma Vibhushan (2001).

NOTE

• Musicians awarded the Bharat Ratna: M. S. Subbulakshmi (1998), Ravi Shankar (1999), Lata Mangeshkar (2001), Bismillah Khan (2001), Bhimsen Joshi (2008).

• Instrument–artist pairs: Sarod – Amjad Ali Khan, Flute – Hariprasad Chaurasia, Sitar – Ravi Shankar, Violin – L. Subramaniam, Sarangi – Ram Narayan.

question: Wightman Cup is associated with which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tennis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Wightman Cup was an annual women’s team tennis competition between the United States and Great Britain, held from 1923 to 1989. (टेनिस)

• It was named after the American player Hazel Hotchkiss Wightman, who donated the trophy.

• Other tennis trophies: Davis Cup (men’s international team event) and the Federation/Billie Jean King Cup (women’s international team event).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Cricket trophies: Ashes, Ranji Trophy, Duleep Trophy, Irani Trophy, Deodhar Trophy, Vijay Hazare Trophy.

• Golf trophies: Ryder Cup, Walker Cup, Solheim Cup, Nomura Trophy.

• Hockey trophies: Agha Khan Cup, Beighton Cup, Dhyan Chand Trophy, Rangaswami Cup, Azlan Shah Cup.

NOTE

• The four tennis Grand Slams: Australian Open (hard), French Open/Roland Garros (clay), Wimbledon (grass) and the US Open (hard).

• Tennis terms: deuce, ace, volley, smash, let, love, tie-breaker.

question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution mentions the fundamental duty “sovereignty, unity and integrity of India” is mentioned?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 51A (c).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 51A(c) lays down the fundamental duty ‘to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India’. (संप्रभुता, एकता और अखंडता)

• Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, and are contained in Part IV-A, Article 51A.

• Originally 10 duties were added; the 11th duty (providing education to children aged 6–14) was inserted by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• 51A(b) — to cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom.

• 51A(d) — to defend the country and render national service when called upon.

• 51A(e) — to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood and renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.

NOTE

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable — they cannot be enforced by courts, unlike Fundamental Rights.

• The idea of Fundamental Duties was borrowed from the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Russia).

• 51A(a) — to abide by the Constitution and respect the National Flag and the National Anthem; 51A(g) — to protect the natural environment.

question: Which among the following gases is used in the artificial ripening of fruits?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Acetylene.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Acetylene (C₂H₂) gas, released when calcium carbide (CaC₂) reacts with moisture, is commonly used for the artificial ripening of fruits such as mangoes and bananas. (कैल्शियम कार्बाइड — मसाला/एसिटिलीन)

• Calcium carbide is popularly called ‘masala’; its use is banned under the Food Safety and Standards Regulations because industrial-grade carbide contains arsenic and phosphorus traces.

• Ethylene (C₂H₄) is the natural plant hormone responsible for ripening, and ethylene gas treatment is the legally permitted method.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Argon is an inert gas used in electric bulbs and welding to prevent oxidation.

• Freon (CFC) is used as a refrigerant and is responsible for ozone layer depletion.

• Helium is a light, non-inflammable gas used in balloons, airships and MRI machines, and mixed with oxygen for divers.

NOTE

• Plant hormones: Auxin (cell elongation), Gibberellin (stem growth), Cytokinin (cell division), Ethylene (ripening), Abscisic acid (stress/dormancy hormone).

• Acetylene is also used in the oxy-acetylene flame for welding and cutting metals.

question: The outer-most range of the Himalayas is called the _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shiwaliks.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Himalayas run in three parallel ranges; the outermost (southernmost) is the Shiwalik (Outer Himalaya), with an average height of 900–1,100 m. (शिवालिक — बाह्य हिमालय)

• The Shiwaliks are made of unconsolidated sediments brought down by rivers; the longitudinal valleys between the Shiwaliks and the Lesser Himalayas are called Duns (e.g., Dehra Dun, Kotli Dun, Patli Dun).

• The three ranges from north to south are Himadri (Greater Himalaya) → Himachal (Lesser Himalaya) → Shiwalik (Outer Himalaya).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Himadri (Greater Himalaya) is the northernmost and highest range, containing Mt. Everest, Kanchenjunga and Nanga Parbat; it is perennially snow-bound.

• Himachal / Himavan (Lesser Himalaya) lies in the middle and includes the Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar and Mahabharat ranges and hill stations like Shimla, Mussoorie and Nainital.

• Konkan is not a Himalayan range — it is the coastal plain of the western coast between Daman and Goa.

NOTE

• Highest peak in India: Kanchenjunga (8,586 m), in Sikkim; K2 (8,611 m) lies in the disputed PoK region.

• Important Himalayan passes: Zoji La (J&K), Rohtang and Shipki La (HP), Nathu La (Sikkim), Bomdi La (Arunachal Pradesh).

question: Who among the following classical dancers was the first person from Odisha to be conferred the Padma Vibhushan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kelucharan Mohapatra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kelucharan Mohapatra (1926–2004) was the legendary Odissi dancer and guru who became the first person from Odisha to be conferred the Padma Vibhushan (2000). (ओडिसी नृत्य)

• He had earlier received the Padma Shri (1972), the Padma Bhushan (1988) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1966).

• He began as a Gotipua dancer and later played a key role in reviving and codifying Odissi, training disciples such as Sanjukta Panigrahi, Sonal Mansingh and Protima Bedi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Pankaj Charan Das is regarded as the ‘father of Odissi’, one of the trinity of Odissi gurus.

• Deba Prasad Das was the third of the great Odissi gurus, known for retaining the tribal and folk elements of the form.

• Raghunath Dutta was an Odissi guru associated with the revival movement in Odisha.

NOTE

• Eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

• Odissi is based on the Natya Shastra and the sculpture of the Konark and Jagannath temples; its themes are drawn from the Gita Govinda of Jayadeva.

question: The music of Bharatanatyam belongs to ______ of southern India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carnatic system.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bharatanatyam, the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, is performed to the Carnatic system of music of southern India. (कर्नाटक संगीत)

• Its accompanying instruments include the mridangam, violin, veena, flute and nattuvangam (cymbals), with the nattuvanar conducting the recital.

• Bharatanatyam evolved from the Sadir/Dasiattam of temple dancers and is based on Bharata Muni’s Natya Shastra; it was revived by Rukmini Devi Arundale, founder of Kalakshetra.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Hindustani system is the classical music of North India, influenced by Persian and Arabic traditions; Kathak is performed to it.

• Purandara Dasa is called the ‘Father of Carnatic music’; the Trinity of Carnatic music are Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri.

• Amir Khusrau is credited with developing forms such as the khayal, tarana and qawwali in Hindustani music.

NOTE

• Carnatic vocal forms: Varnam, Kriti, Ragam-Tanam-Pallavi; Hindustani forms: Dhrupad, Dhamar, Khayal, Thumri, Tappa.

• Famous Bharatanatyam exponents: Rukmini Devi Arundale, Balasaraswati, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Padma Subrahmanyam, Mallika Sarabhai.

question: Which disease is caused by the deficiency of protein in the diet?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kwashiorkor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kwashiorkor is a protein-energy malnutrition disease caused by a severe deficiency of protein with adequate calories, seen mainly in children aged 1–5 years. (प्रोटीन की कमी)

• Its symptoms are oedema (swelling) of the legs and face, a protruding belly, stunted growth, thin hair and skin patches.

• Marasmus, in contrast, is caused by a deficiency of both protein and calories, and leads to extreme wasting without oedema.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Rickets is caused by a deficiency of Vitamin D (bone deformity in children); in adults it causes osteomalacia.

• Scurvy is caused by a deficiency of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) and leads to bleeding gums.

• Jaundice is a liver disorder marked by an excess of bilirubin, not a nutritional deficiency disease.

NOTE

• Deficiency diseases: Vitamin A – night blindness, Vitamin B1 – beriberi, Vitamin B3 – pellagra, Vitamin B12 – pernicious anaemia, Vitamin K – delayed blood clotting, Iron – anaemia, Iodine – goitre.

• Proteins are the body-building foods; they are made of amino acids, of which 9 are essential for humans.

question: Power of High Courts to issue certain writs is included under which article of the Indian constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 226.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 226 empowers every High Court to issue writs — habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari and quo warranto — for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose. (रिट अधिकारिता)

• The writ jurisdiction of the High Court is wider than that of the Supreme Court, whose power under Article 32 is limited to the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

• Article 32 was called the ‘heart and soul of the Constitution’ by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Article 220 — restriction on practice after being a permanent judge of a High Court.

• Article 222 — transfer of a judge from one High Court to another by the President after consulting the CJI.

• Article 224 — appointment of additional and acting judges of a High Court.

NOTE

• Meaning of writs: Habeas corpus – ‘to have the body’; Mandamus – ‘we command’; Prohibition – ‘to forbid’ (issued to lower courts); Certiorari – ‘to be certified’; Quo warranto – ‘by what authority’.

• High Courts are dealt with in Part VI, Articles 214–231; Article 214 provides a High Court for each state.

question: Sri-Lanka is separated from India by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Palk strait.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sri Lanka is separated from India by the Palk Strait and the Gulf of Mannar; the strait links the Bay of Bengal with the Gulf of Mannar. (पाक जलडमरूमध्य)

• A chain of shoals between Rameswaram (Dhanushkodi) in India and Mannar Island in Sri Lanka is called Adam’s Bridge / Ram Setu.

• The strait is named after Robert Palk, a Governor of Madras; Kachchatheevu island lies in this area and was ceded to Sri Lanka in 1974.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Strait of Gibraltar connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Atlantic Ocean, separating Spain from Morocco.

• Strait of Malacca lies between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra (Indonesia), one of the world’s busiest shipping lanes.

• Bering Strait separates Asia (Russia) from North America (Alaska) and connects the Arctic Ocean with the Pacific.

NOTE

• India’s southernmost point on the mainland is Kanyakumari; the southernmost point of Indian territory is Indira Point in the Great Nicobar Island.

• The Ten Degree Channel separates the Andaman and Nicobar islands; the Nine Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the Lakshadweep group.

question: Who among the following is the author of ‘River of Smoke’ novel?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amitav Ghosh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• ‘River of Smoke’ (2011) is a novel by Amitav Ghosh, the second book of his Ibis Trilogy. (इबिस त्रयी)

• The trilogy comprises ‘Sea of Poppies’ (2008), ‘River of Smoke’ (2011) and ‘Flood of Fire’ (2015), set around the opium trade and the First Opium War.

• Amitav Ghosh was awarded the Jnanpith Award in 2018 — the first English-language writer in India to receive it — and the Sahitya Akademi Award (1989) for ‘The Shadow Lines’.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• B. B. Lal was a noted archaeologist, former Director-General of the ASI, author of ‘The Sarasvati Flows On’.

• Jeet Thayil wrote ‘Narcopolis’ (2012), shortlisted for the Man Booker Prize.

• Manohar Malgonkar wrote ‘A Bend in the Ganges’ and ‘The Princes’.

NOTE

• Other works of Amitav Ghosh: ‘The Circle of Reason’, ‘The Glass Palace’, ‘The Hungry Tide’, ‘Gun Island’, ‘The Great Derangement’, ‘The Nutmeg’s Curse’.

• The Jnanpith Award, instituted in 1961, is India’s highest literary honour.

question: Which Lodi ruler's (1489 AD -1517 AD) real name was Nizam Khan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sikandar Lodi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sikandar Lodi (r. 1489–1517), whose real name was Nizam Khan, was the second and ablest ruler of the Lodi dynasty. (सिकंदर लोदी — निज़ाम खान)

• He founded the city of Agra in 1504 and shifted his capital there from Delhi.

• He wrote Persian verses under the pen name ‘Gulrukhi’ and introduced the Gaz-i-Sikandari, a measuring yard for land.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Bahlul Lodi (1451–1489) founded the Lodi dynasty, the last dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, and was of Afghan origin.

• Ibrahim Lodi (1517–1526) was the last Lodi ruler; he was defeated and killed by Babur in the First Battle of Panipat (1526).

• Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah belonged to the Khalji dynasty, not the Lodis.

NOTE

• Five dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526): Slave/Mamluk (1206), Khalji (1290), Tughlaq (1320), Sayyid (1414) and Lodi (1451).

• The Lodi Gardens in Delhi contain the tombs of Sikandar Lodi and Mohammed Shah Sayyid.

question: How many Indian states celebrate their formation on November 1ˢᵗ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seven.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Seven Indian states celebrate their formation day on 1 November — Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana and Chhattisgarh. (राज्य स्थापना दिवस — 1 नवंबर)

• Kerala, Karnataka (then Mysore), Andhra Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh were formed on 1 November 1956 under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, which redrew state boundaries on a linguistic basis.

• Punjab and Haryana were reorganised on 1 November 1966 under the Punjab Reorganisation Act, and Chhattisgarh was created out of Madhya Pradesh on 1 November 2000.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Andhra Pradesh (1953) was the first state formed on a linguistic basis, after the death of Potti Sriramulu.

• The States Reorganisation Commission (1953) was headed by Fazl Ali, with K. M. Panikkar and H. N. Kunzru as members.

• Other states formed in 2000: Uttarakhand (9 November) and Jharkhand (15 November); Telangana was formed on 2 June 2014.

NOTE

• Article 3 of the Constitution empowers Parliament to form new states and alter the areas, boundaries or names of existing states.

• The Dhar Committee (1948) and the JVP Committee (1949 — Nehru, Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya) initially opposed reorganisation purely on linguistic lines.
